title: The Iron Curtain Speech (1946): The Dawn of the Cold War
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: 'From Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic, an iron curtain has descended across the Continent', warned Churchill, defining modern geopolitical strategy.
keywords: The Iron Curtain Speech (1946): The Dawn of the Cold War
full_text:
On March 5, 1946, in the small town of Fulton, Missouri, Winston Churchill delivered one of the most consequential geopolitical speeches in world history: **The Sinews of Peace**.

With President Harry S. Truman seated beside him on the auditorium stage, Churchill warned the world that the defeat of Nazi Germany had given rise to a new totalitarian threat from Moscow:

"From Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic, an **iron curtain** has descended across the Continent!
Behind that line lie all the capitals of the ancient states of Central and Eastern Europe: Warsaw, Berlin, Prague, Vienna, Budapest, Belgrade, Bucharest, and Sofia—all these famous cities and their populations lie subject to Soviet control."

Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin immediately denounced Churchill as a warmonger.

When asked why he broke alliance with Moscow, Churchill explained:
"We allied with the bear to defeat the crocodile of Nazism. But now the crocodile is dead, and the bear seeks to devour us.
One cannot appease a tyrant; an appeaser is merely one who feeds a crocodile, hoping it will eat him last!"

Churchill's prophetic phrase 'Iron Curtain' defined world politics for the next half-century, giving birth to the Atlantic Alliance and NATO.
moral: Appeasement never satisfies totalitarian aggression; moral vigilance and early deterrence are the true guarantees of peace.
